content: Transferability in chemistry refers to the concept that a specific chemical property associated with an atom or a functional group within a molecule tends to exhibit a similar, though not necessarily identical, value across different chemical environments. Additionally, chemical shifts observed in nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, which provide information about the electronic environment of nuclei, and characteristic vibrational frequencies detected in infrared (IR) spectroscopy, which correspond to specific bond vibrations, are also examples of transferable properties. It is important to distinguish transferable properties from conserved properties. Conserved properties, such as relative atomic mass, are assumed to remain constant regardless of the chemical context or environment.
